title: Risk Assessment: Full DAG visualization for Tier 3 parallel phase execution
summary: Assessment of the proposed Approach A (expand Implement phase into sub-phase boxes in render_pipeline_dag) for rendering Tier 3 parallel plan phase execution as a branching DAG. The change is concentrated in orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py with no model or schema changes, and downstream consumers (SSE, CLI tools, API) require zero changes. The overall risk is Low-Medium. Seven risks identified: one Medium (contract loading path discovery), four Low-Medium, and two Low. The most significant design gap is that render_pipeline_dag() currently has no way to discover the contract file path, since the Pipeline model lacks a repo_root/worktree_path field and the function signature is constrained. This must be resolved before implementation begins. All other risks are mitigable with the architect's proposed fallback-to-flat strategy and thorough unit testing.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with Approach A. The change is well-scoped: all visualization logic is in dag_visualizer.py, no model changes, no orchestrator dispatch changes, and all downstream consumers are decoupled (they consume text output). The primary risks are: (1) a design gap around contract file path discovery that must be resolved in Phase 1, and (2) the inherent complexity of multi-column ASCII text composition. Both are solvable with the approaches described below. The fallback-to-flat strategy ensures the visualizer never degrades — if anything goes wrong loading the contract or computing waves, the existing single-Implement-box rendering is used.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of dag_visualizer.py (665 lines, all functions), models.py (Pipeline, AgentExecution.plan_phase_id, ComplexityTier), shared/egg_contracts/dependency_graph.py (PhaseDependencyGraph.compute_waves, PhaseWave), shared/egg_contracts/loader.py (load_contract), orchestrator/sse.py (SSE refresh cycle calling render_pipeline_dag every 1s), orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (_run_tier3_implement contract loading pattern), and orchestrator/tests/test_dag_visualizer.py (1313 lines, 13 test classes)

risks.title: Contract loading path unknown in render_pipeline_dag() context
risks.description: The architect's _get_phase_dependency_info() function needs to call load_contract(issue_number, repo_root) to load the contract's phase structure. However, render_pipeline_dag() only receives a Pipeline object, and the Pipeline model (models.py:235-279) has no repo_root or worktree_repo_path field. The function signature constraint (architect's constraint #6: 'The render_pipeline_dag() function signature must not change') means repo_root cannot be passed as a parameter without violating the design. The _run_tier3_implement() dispatch function (pipelines.py:2696) receives worktree_repo_path as a parameter from the dispatch flow, but the SSE code (sse.py:241) calls render_pipeline_dag(pipeline, use_ascii=use_ascii) with no path context. This is a guaranteed issue that must be resolved before implementation can begin.

steps: Option A (preferred): Add an optional repo_root parameter to render_pipeline_dag(). This is a minimal signature change — existing callers pass nothing and get the fallback behavior. The SSE code can derive the worktree path from the pipeline_id using the orchestrator's known worktree directory convention (the orchestrator creates worktrees in a known base directory). This is the cleanest solution since it preserves backward compatibility while enabling contract loading.

Option B: Use environment variable (EGG_REPO_PATH) in _get_phase_dependency_info(). The orchestrator process has this set. Downside: only works for single-repo deployments and doesn't handle per-pipeline worktrees correctly.

Option C: Add worktree_path to the Pipeline model. This is the most correct solution long-term but constitutes a model migration. Existing pipelines in flight would have None for the field. Since the architect explicitly excluded model changes, this option conflicts with the recommended approach.

Recommendation: Use Option A. Adding an optional parameter with a default of None is backward-compatible and lets the SSE code pass the worktree path if available, or let _get_phase_dependency_info() fall back to environment/convention-based path discovery. The constraint against signature changes should be relaxed — adding an optional parameter with a default is safe.
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — with Option A, callers that don't pass repo_root get flat rendering (current behavior), while callers that do pass it get the new Tier 3 visualization.

risks.review_reason: The architect's constraint #6 ('function signature must not change') conflicts with the need to pass repo_root for contract loading. Human should decide whether to relax this constraint (Option A) or accept environment-variable-based path discovery (Option B).

risks.title: Contract loading in the SSE hot path adds file I/O to every render cycle
risks.description: render_pipeline_dag() is called every 1 second by the SSE refresh cycle (sse.py:241-249) for each connected client. The DAG cache (sse.py:237) avoids redundant renders for clients with the same use_ascii preference, but each render still calls _get_phase_dependency_info() which would load_contract() — reading a JSON file from disk and parsing it, then constructing PhaseDependencyGraph and computing waves. For a typical contract (~5-20KB JSON), this adds ~1-5ms per render cycle. With N concurrent SSE clients (each pipeline gets its own refresh), this scales as O(pipelines). While the compare-before-send optimization (sse.py, comparing rendered strings) doesn't help here — the rendering itself is the expensive part, not the sending.

mitigation.strategy: In-memory cache with TTL or invalidation
steps: Cache the computed (phase_waves, phase_info) tuple keyed by (pipeline_id, contract_mtime) using functools.lru_cache or a simple dict with TTL
The contract file only changes when the plan phase rewrites it — during implementation, it's static. A 30-second TTL would be sufficient.
Alternatively, use os.stat().st_mtime to check if the file changed before re-parsing. This replaces a ~5ms JSON parse with a ~0.1ms stat call.
For the initial implementation, even without caching, 1-5ms per render is acceptable for the 1s refresh interval. Caching is an optimization that can be added if profiling shows a problem.
If caching is added, ensure it's per-pipeline (not global) to avoid cross-pipeline data leaks.
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — even without caching, the overhead is small relative to the 1s refresh interval. With mtime-based caching, overhead is negligible.

risks.title: Side-by-side ASCII box composition is error-prone and hard to test visually
risks.description: The _render_side_by_side() function must horizontally compose multiple variable-height text boxes, handling: (1) padding shorter boxes to match the tallest, (2) inserting consistent gap spacing between columns, (3) ensuring each line has the same total width for clean vertical alignment, (4) handling boxes with different internal widths. Additionally, _render_fan_out_connector() and _render_fan_in_connector() must compute precise character positions for branching lines that align with the center of each box in the side-by-side layout. The connector math depends on box widths, gap size, and left margin — any off-by-one error produces visually broken connectors. Unicode box-drawing characters and ASCII fallback characters have different visual properties but the same character width (1), so alignment math is at least consistent.

steps: Normalize all sub-phase boxes in a parallel wave to the same width (max width in the wave). This eliminates variable-width connector math and produces cleaner visual output.
Implement _render_side_by_side as a pure function that takes pre-rendered line lists and returns combined lines. Test it independently with known inputs before integrating.
Use snapshot/golden-file tests for the connector functions: render with known inputs and assert exact string output. This catches off-by-one errors immediately.
Start with 2-column rendering and verify before generalizing to N columns. Most Tier 3 pipelines have 2-3 parallel phases per wave.
Test both Unicode and ASCII modes — each has different character sets but the same alignment math.
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — rendering bugs are cosmetic, not functional. The pipeline continues to work correctly even if the visualization has alignment issues. Snapshot tests catch regressions early.

risks.title: Tier 3 detection false positive breaks Tier 1/2 visualization
risks.description: The Tier 3 detection logic checks (1) pipeline.complexity_tier == ComplexityTier.HIGH and (2) agents in the Implement phase have plan_phase_id set. If only condition (1) is checked (e.g., due to a bug or incomplete implementation), a HIGH-tier pipeline whose agents don't have plan_phase_id (e.g., if the plan phase ran but no Tier 3 dispatch happened due to an error) would trigger the Tier 3 rendering path with no sub-phase data, producing an empty or broken visualization. Conversely, if plan_phase_id is set on agents of a non-HIGH pipeline (shouldn't happen but data may be inconsistent), the detection could trigger unexpectedly.

mitigation.strategy: Strict dual-condition check with explicit fallback
steps: Both conditions MUST be true for Tier 3 rendering: complexity_tier == HIGH AND at least one agent has plan_phase_id set AND _get_phase_dependency_info() returns non-None (contract loads successfully with valid waves).
If _get_phase_dependency_info() returns None (contract missing, no phases, wave computation fails), fall back to flat rendering regardless of complexity_tier.

Add explicit unit tests for: (a) HIGH tier with plan_phase_id -> Tier 3 rendering, (b) HIGH tier without plan_phase_id -> flat rendering, (c) MID tier with plan_phase_id (shouldn't happen) -> flat rendering, (d) HIGH tier with contract load failure -> flat rendering.
The detection logic should be a single function (_is_tier3_pipeline) to centralize the check and make it testable.
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — triple-condition check (tier + plan_phase_id + contract available) makes false positives extremely unlikely.

risks.title: Contract unavailability during SSE rendering across pipeline lifecycle
risks.description: The SSE refresh renders the DAG for pipelines in ALL phases, not just Implement. During Refine and early Plan phases, the contract file may not exist yet (it's created during plan phase). During error states, the contract may be corrupted or have no phases array. The _get_phase_dependency_info() function calls load_contract() which raises ContractNotFoundError if the file is missing (loader.py:78). If this exception propagates uncaught, it would crash render_pipeline_dag() and produce no DAG output for that SSE refresh cycle. The SSE code (sse.py:242-249) has a try/except around render_pipeline_dag that catches any exception and sets dag_cache to None, but this means NO visualization is sent, not even the flat fallback.

steps: _get_phase_dependency_info() must wrap ALL contract loading in try/except and return None on any error (ContractNotFoundError, JSON decode errors, missing 'phases' field, PhaseDependencyGraph ValueError for cycles, etc.)
When _get_phase_dependency_info() returns None, render_pipeline_dag() falls back to the existing flat Implement box rendering — NOT to no output.
Add a log.debug() (not warning) for contract load failures during rendering, since they are expected during non-Implement phases.
Unit test: call render_pipeline_dag() with a Tier 3 Pipeline but no contract on disk — verify it produces valid output (the flat Implement box).
Ensure the exception is caught INSIDE dag_visualizer.py, not relying on the SSE caller's broad except. The SSE except should be a safety net, not the primary error handler.
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — with return-None-on-error, the visualizer always produces output. The SSE safety net catches anything else.

risks.title: No existing test infrastructure for Tier 3 sub-phase branching — tests must be built from scratch
risks.description: test_dag_visualizer.py (1313 lines) has 13 test classes but no tests for Tier 3 sub-phase visualization. The existing TestWaveGrouping class tests wave-based agent ordering within a flat phase box, not multi-box branching. The test helper create_test_pipeline() creates a Pipeline with issue_number=123 — tests for contract loading need either a real contract file on disk or a mock. The PhaseDependencyGraph is in shared/egg_contracts/ which has its own test file — the visualizer tests should mock it rather than testing the graph computation. The new test classes (TestTier3DagVisualization, TestSideBySideRendering, TestFanOutFanInConnectors as proposed by the architect) need to be comprehensive since there's no existing coverage to fall back on.

steps: Mock _get_phase_dependency_info() to return known PhaseWave structures, avoiding filesystem dependencies in tests.

Create helper functions for building test Tier 3 pipelines: create_tier3_pipeline(phases=[('phase-1', [agents...]), ('phase-2', [agents...])]) that sets complexity_tier=HIGH and assigns plan_phase_id to agents.
Use snapshot testing (exact string comparison) for rendered DAG output. Snapshot failures are easy to review visually.
Test matrix should cover: 1 sequential phase, 2 parallel phases, 3 parallel phases, diamond pattern (seq->parallel->seq), mixed waves, all-complete status, mixed status, ASCII mode, empty agents.
Run the existing test suite FIRST to establish a baseline, then add new tests. Verify existing tests still pass after the change.
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — comprehensive test suite eliminates most regression risk. The test-first approach (add tests before modifying rendering) catches regressions immediately.

risks.title: Terminal width overflow for pipelines with 4+ parallel sub-phases
risks.description: Each sub-phase box has a minimum width of ~25 characters (phase name + agent names + status symbols + box borders). With a 4-character gap between columns, 4 parallel boxes need (25*4 + 4*3 + left_margin) = ~116 characters. With 5+ parallel boxes, this exceeds the 120-column default for SSE contexts and the 80-column default for terminals. The architect proposes falling back to sequential (stacked) rendering for 4+ phases, but this fallback needs implementation and testing. Without it, rendered lines would wrap or be truncated, producing garbled output.

steps: Compute required width before rendering side-by-side. If total_width > available_width, fall back to stacked rendering with a '(parallel)' label.
Use shutil.get_terminal_size(fallback=(120, 24)) for width detection. The fallback covers SSE contexts (not a TTY).
For the common case (2-3 parallel phases), the side-by-side layout fits comfortably in 120 columns. The 4+ case is rare — most Tier 3 plans have 2-3 independent phases per wave.
As a future enhancement, a 2-row grid layout (2 boxes per row) could handle 4-6 phases, but this is not needed for the initial implementation.
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — the stacked fallback preserves all information, just without the visual side-by-side structure.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: R-1 — The architect's constraint that 'render_pipeline_dag() function signature must not change' conflicts with the need to pass repo_root for contract loading. Human should decide whether to (a) relax this constraint by adding an optional repo_root parameter, (b) derive the path from environment variables, or (c) add repo_root to the Pipeline model. This decision affects the Phase 1 implementation approach.

areas_requiring_human_review.area: Visual output review of rendered Tier 3 DAGs
areas_requiring_human_review.reason: R-3, R-7 — Side-by-side ASCII rendering is inherently visual. Automated tests can verify exact string output, but a human should visually inspect the rendered DAGs for common patterns (2-column, 3-column, diamond, mixed sequential/parallel) to confirm they are readable and aesthetically reasonable.

rollback_plan.strategy: Simple revert — no schema or data changes
rollback_plan.details: The change is entirely within dag_visualizer.py (visualization logic) and its test file. No model changes, no schema migrations, no persisted state changes. The Pipeline model, contract format, and SSE protocol are unchanged.
steps: If the new visualization has bugs: revert the commits to dag_visualizer.py. All downstream consumers (SSE, CLI tools, API) continue working with the flat rendering.
If only specific edge cases are broken: the fallback-to-flat logic means the Tier 3 path can be disabled by making _get_phase_dependency_info() always return None (one-line change).
No data migration needed — the contract format is unchanged and the Pipeline model is unchanged.
The rollback does not affect pipeline execution — visualization is purely cosmetic.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Resolve the contract loading path discovery (R-1) before starting Phase 1
implementation_recommendations.rationale: This is a design decision that affects the function signature and calling convention. The implementation team should decide on Option A (add optional repo_root param) vs Option B (environment variable) upfront, since it affects how _get_phase_dependency_info() is implemented and tested.

This function is the single point of failure for the Tier 3 path. If it raises an exception, the visualization breaks. Wrapping ALL logic in try/except with return None ensures the flat fallback always works. Log errors at debug level since contract-not-found is expected during non-Implement phases.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Normalize sub-phase box widths before computing connector positions
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Variable-width boxes make connector math significantly harder. If all boxes in a parallel wave are padded to the same width, the fan-out/fan-in connector positions are symmetric and trivial to compute. This simplification eliminates an entire class of alignment bugs.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Add caching to _get_phase_dependency_info() using file mtime comparison
implementation_recommendations.rationale: The SSE refresh calls render_pipeline_dag() every 1 second. Caching the parsed contract data with mtime-based invalidation reduces the per-render overhead from ~5ms (file read + JSON parse + graph computation) to ~0.1ms (stat call). This is a simple optimization that prevents performance concerns from materializing.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Use snapshot testing for all rendered DAG outputs
implementation_recommendations.rationale: ASCII art rendering is best tested by exact string comparison. Snapshot tests (comparing rendered output against known-good baselines) catch off-by-one alignment errors, missing connectors, and width overflow issues that would be invisible to structural assertions.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Implement Phase 1 (sequential sub-phases) and validate before adding parallel rendering
implementation_recommendations.rationale: The architect's phased approach is sound. Phase 1 (sequential sub-phases only) validates the contract loading, Tier 3 detection, and sub-phase box rendering without the complexity of side-by-side composition. This provides a working intermediate state and reduces risk.

phase_1.name: Core rendering helpers and single-column Tier 3 visualization
phase_1.rationale: Phase 1 adds contract loading to the visualizer (new dependency) and modifies render_pipeline_dag() (shared code path). However, the Tier 3 detection with fallback-to-flat means existing pipelines are unaffected. The key risk is R-1 (contract loading path) which must be resolved first. Sequential sub-phase rendering is simpler than parallel since no side-by-side composition is needed.

phase_2.name: Side-by-side parallel rendering with fan-out/fan-in connectors
phase_2.rationale: Phase 2 adds the most complex new code (side-by-side composition, connector rendering). The risk is concentrated in visual rendering logic that doesn't affect pipeline execution. The fallback for 4+ parallel phases (R-7) needs implementation. Since Phase 1 already validates the contract loading and Tier 3 detection, Phase 2 only needs to add the parallel layout on top of a working sequential layout.

compatibility_assessment.schema_changes: None — no model or data schema changes
compatibility_assessment.api_changes: None — generate_status_report() return structure unchanged (dag field contains new text, but structure is identical)
compatibility_assessment.breaking_changes: None — Tier 1/2 pipelines render identically. Tier 3 pipelines get improved visualization with flat-rendering fallback.

security_assessment.details: This change only affects ASCII text rendering of pipeline state. It does not modify authentication, authorization, file access controls, gateway enforcement, or any security boundary. The new contract loading reads from .egg-state/contracts/ which is already accessed by the orchestrator. No user input is processed differently. The PhaseDependencyGraph operates on trusted data from the contract file.
